requirements.quote: A check on a new party finds existing matters where the chamber appears for an adverse party, including transliterated names.
The feature is behind a flag until counsel signs off (#486).
`packages/core/src/conflicts/`: name matching (transliteration-aware for Tamil and Kannada, organisation aliases) against the chamber's matters and parties, and optionally its cause-list history.
`apps/web`: a conflict check on new-matter intake, showing results with sources; it never auto-blocks, and the advocate decides.
Audit: every check is logged; no data leaves the chamber's workspace.

requirements.why: Optional in the issue; `listing` (packages/db/src/schema/docket.ts:50) carries no party names, so history matching needs a separate data source and counsel review of processing cause-list parties. Follow-up issue.

deliverables.change: Name normaliser: NFKC, case-fold, strip honorifics (Sri/Smt/Dr/M/S) and company suffixes (Pvt Ltd/Limited), organisation alias table, Tamil (U+0B80-0BFF) and Kannada (U+0C80-0CFF) to Latin phonetic key, collapse vowel length/aspirates/doubled letters, token-order independent key.

checkConflicts(deps, actor, input): loads person/organisation (name+aliases) and role_edge to matters inside the caller's workspace transaction; a hit is a new adverse party equal to an existing client, or a new client equal to an existing adverse party; returns hits with matter id/title, matched name, role and source; always records one audit event (ids and counts, no names); never touches network or other workspaces.
Domain barrel exporting checkConflicts, normaliser and types.
Add `./conflicts` export mirroring `./case-watch` (line 22). No dependency changes.
Export the conflicts domain as the other domains are exported.
Register `conflict.checked` audit action (security:true so a check cannot run unlogged).
Add the `conflicts.check` row (⚖, KILL_CONFLICTS_CHECK, #500) to match the registry.
Add `checkConflictsAction` (workspaceAction, `matter.read`, requireFlag('conflicts.check') -> NOT_FOUND when off) calling core checkConflicts.
Optional conflict-check step on intake: when the flag is on, show hits with sources; submission is never blocked, the advocate decides.
Conflict check strings under matters.new (also kn and ta matters.json and the generated message files, per the i18n catalog test).
Add conflicts row, dependency table row and graph edge.
SERVICE_TESTS entry for checkConflicts (workspace B check sees nothing of A) and NOT_A_SERVICE for pure normaliser exports.
Real case: B checking A's client name gets no hits; A's data unchanged.
Register checkConflictsAction in ACTIONS with probe input.
Integration test (R1: adverse party matches existing client incl. Tamil/Kannada spelling vs Latin, organisation alias, no hit across workspaces, audit event written) and normaliser unit tests.
Unit test: action returns NOT_FOUND with flag off, results with flag on; legal-gated flag registered (R2).

preserve.what: createMatterAction behaviour and result shape (apps/web/app/(app)/w/[slug]/matters/actions.ts:50): the conflict check must never block or alter matter creation.
Flag precedence and legal-ack rules (packages/flags/src/evaluate.ts:47-60); every flag default stays false.
Tenant isolation: no cross-workspace reads, no new SECURITY DEFINER function, no migration.
Existing audit action registry entries and AUDIT_ACTIONS shape (packages/core/src/audit/events.ts).

validate.command: pnpm --filter @causedeck/core exec vitest run src/conflicts src/__tests__/cross-tenant/services.test.ts src/domains.test.ts --maxWorkers=${FORGE_HOST_PARALLELISM:-2}

decisions.choice: No migration and no SECURITY DEFINER function: the check runs entirely inside the caller's withWorkspace transaction over tenant tables.
decisions.justification: Tenant tables are FORCE RLS (packages/db/src/schema/people.ts:1-3), which satisfies 'no data leaves the chamber's workspace' by construction.

decisions.choice: Self-contained Tamil/Kannada phonetic normaliser in core instead of a new dependency.
decisions.justification: No transliteration library exists in the repo (advocate-keys.ts:3-5 keeps names raw); avoids a new package dependency.
Issue requires every check logged; fail-closed (packages/core/src/audit/events.ts:1-5) guarantees a check cannot run unaudited.

decisions.choice: Core conflicts depends only on audit; matter/person rows are read directly with the caller's tx.
decisions.justification: CORE_DOMAIN_DEPENDENCIES rule (packages/config/eslint/core-domains.js) allows only registered imports via index.ts.
